macro.text: Meta announces a $95 billion stock offering to fund its AI expansion.
Neocloud stocks fall after Elon Musk says more than 200 of them face "guppy-level death".
Trump says he will soon decide whether to "make a deal" with Iran or "finish it off".
Verizon lifts its annual forecasts and signs a more than $2 billion AI infrastructure deal with AWS.
Goldman cuts its Kospi forecast by 25%, a read-through for the global AI trade.
Oil slides over 2% as traders weigh Saudi attack risks and demand destruction.

briefs.read: The tone is mixed with a mild risk-on lean in tech: QQQ is up about 0.7% premarket while SPY is roughly flat, the VIX closed Friday a little lower near 19, and WTI is down about 2% to around $101, though the 10-year yield is slightly higher near 4.99%. There are no high-impact scheduled releases today, so the day has no single data event; the main items are company and headline driven, chiefly how the market takes Meta's $95 billion stock offering and the pressure on neocloud and AI infrastructure names. Iran is the open geopolitical risk, with Trump saying a decision on a deal or further action is coming soon, and any headline there could move oil and the indexes quickly. Before taking a setup, it is worth waiting for the first 15-minute range to form and seeing whether QQQ's premarket strength holds once Meta and the AI names trade at the open.

macro.text: Brazilian stocks are rocked after Lula wins the presidential runoff; Bolsonaro reportedly refuses to concede.
Anthropic files its prospectus, starting the countdown to a blockbuster IPO.
Oil falls as the Saudi defense minister travels to Iran for talks aimed at de-escalating the conflict.

briefs.read: The open held and broadened the morning's mild risk-on tone: SPY, roughly flat premarket at 763.13, is now 765.15 (+0.68% on the day, +0.38% since the 9:30 open near 762.2), and QQQ is 709.49 (+0.72%, +0.34% since the open near 707.1), only a touch above its 709.22 premarket print, so tech's early lead has been joined rather than extended. The VIX is down about 4% to 18.63, the 10-year yield has eased to 4.97% from about 4.99% premarket, and WTI is down about 1.8% at $101.43 but roughly flat since the open after news of Saudi-Iran de-escalation talks. There are no high-impact scheduled releases left today, so the remaining drivers are headlines: Iran, how Meta's $95 billion offering and the AI infrastructure names trade, and the Anthropic IPO filing.

The morning's mild risk-on tone is still holding but has stalled since 10:00: SPY is 764.66 (+0.62% on the day, +0.32% since the 9:30 open near 762.2), a little below its 765.15 at 10:17 and above the 763.13 premarket print, while QQQ is unchanged at 709.53 (+0.73%, +0.35% since the open near 707.1), just above its 709.22 premarket level. The VIX has kept easing to 18.17 (down about 6.6% on the day and 3% since the open), the 10-year yield is a touch lower at 4.97%, and WTI has slipped just under $101 (down about 2.2%, -0.6% since the open). There are still no high-impact scheduled releases today, so the drivers remain headlines: Iran, Meta's $95 billion offering and the AI infrastructure names, and the Anthropic IPO filing.

macro.text: Stocks close higher as excitement over the Anthropic IPO filing lifts the tech sector.
The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady at its October meeting.
Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom could buy Meta shares as part of its stock offering.
Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees in an AI-driven efficiency push.

briefs.read: The morning read held: it expected a mixed tone with a mild risk-on lean in tech and no scheduled data, and the day closed that way, with QQQ up 1.18% at 712.69 (+0.80% since the 9:30 open near 707.0) clearly ahead of SPY's +0.69% at 765.19 (+0.39% since the open near 762.2). There was no high-impact U.S. release today, so headlines drove the session; closing coverage credits the Anthropic IPO filing with lifting tech, and Meta's stock offering did not hold back the Nasdaq-heavy gains. The biggest change came after the 10:30 update: SPY stayed near 765, about where it was at 10:17, while QQQ climbed from about 709.5 at 10:35 to 712.69 at the close, though these snapshots cannot show exactly when that move happened. The VIX finished down about 5.5% at 18.39, a little above its 18.17 reading at 10:20, WTI held near $101 (down 1.8%), and the 10-year yield ended little changed near 4.99%. For tomorrow's preparation, note that tech carried the day while SPY went flat after mid-morning, and the Fed decision later this week, where a hold is widely expected, is the next big U.S. scheduled event. Tomorrow's first red event is Australian CPI at 8:30 PM ET; no U.S. high-impact releases are listed for Tuesday.
